proved_step:
REPAIR LEMMA (class match for MMW19 Thm 1.3):

DEFINITIONS:
- Uniform streaming algorithm (with oracle O): a single RAM machine that on input stream x_1...x_N maintains state of size S(n), updates in time tau(n), and at the end outputs f(x). The machine may query oracle O during computation.
- Nonuniform exact staged Boolean realization (MMW19 Def.): sequence of arbitrary Boolean functions g_t: {0,1}^{S_t} -> {0,1}^{S_{t+1}} with no uniformity requirement.
- MMW19 Thm 1.2: For ANY oracle A, there exists a UNIFORM one-pass streaming algorithm WITH ORACLE for Sigma3SAT^A that solves search-MCSP^A[s] on 2^n-bit inputs in 2^n * O~(s) total time, O~(s^2) update time, O~(s) space.
- MMW19 Thm 1.3: Let s(n) time-constructible, s(n) >= n, A in PH. If search-MCSP^A[s] has NO uniform one-pass streaming algorithm (WITHOUT oracle) with poly(s) space and poly(s) update time, then P != NP.
  Proof given: Assume P=NP. By Thm 1.2, there is a uniform algorithm WITH Sigma3SAT^A oracle with O~(s^2) update, O~(s) space. Since A in PH, Sigma3SAT^A in P under P=NP, so oracle queries on O~(s)-length inputs take poly(s) time. Simulating the oracle yields a UNIFORM algorithm WITHOUT oracle with poly(s) space and poly(s) update time. Contradiction.

CLASS MATCH: Thm 1.3's hypothesis quantifies over UNIFORM oracle-free one-pass streaming algorithms. The algorithm constructed under P=NP is also UNIFORM (the Thm 1.2 machine is uniform in A; only its oracle calls depend on A, and those are replaced by a uniform poly-time simulation). Therefore the class match holds: MMW's quantified class = uniform oracle-free one-pass streaming algorithms.

CONSEQUENCE for (40a): The manuscript's (40a) quantifies over M_{s,A}^plain = uniform deterministic one-pass RAM algorithms WITHOUT oracle. This EXACTLY matches MMW Thm 1.3's hypothesis class. Therefore (40a) => H (no such algorithm exists) => P!=NP via MMW Thm 1.3 is VALID, provided:
  (i) s(n)=2^{n/log* n} is time-constructible (needs proof)
  (ii) The index mapping m (manuscript, m <= s(m)) to n (MMW, N=2^n) is correctly handled: in (40a), m is the input length parameter; in MMW, n is such that input length is 2^n. So m = 2^n. The condition m <= s(m) becomes 2^n <= s(2^n). For s(n)=2^{n/log* n}, we need s(2^n) = 2^{2^n / log* 2^n}. This is a different function. The manuscript must use a consistent parameterization.

This lemma REPAIRS the refuted S0002 by establishing the class match. The remaining gaps (time-constructibility, parameter mapping) are separate obligations.

proved_step: Repaired quantifier lemma (same-class scope). Let C be any fixed class of machines and let b(M,c,d,m) denote [S_M(m) > s(m)^c or tau_M(m) > s(m)^d]. If (40a) is read as forall M in C, forall c,d, forall m0, exists m >= m0: b(M,c,d,m), then there is no M in C and no fixed c,d for which both bounds hold for every sufficiently large m. Proof: suppose such M,c,d exist, with threshold m1. Apply (40a) to that M,c,d and m0=m1. Its witness m >= m1 has b(M,c,d,m) true, contradicting the assumed two bounds at every m >= m1. Conversely, if no such eventual-fast triple exists, then for each M,c,d and each m0 there must be some m >= m0 where at least one bound fails; otherwise both bounds hold for all m >= m0. Thus the two formulations are equivalent for the same quantified class C. This repairs only the quantifier step: it does not transfer from C to a different MMW machine class.

statement: Conditional resource-transfer lemma. Let s:N→N satisfy s(m)≥m. Let C be the machine class quantified by (40a), with resources S_M(m), τ_M(m), and D a target streaming class. Assume every T∈D has a simulator M_T∈C and constants a,b,r≥1 such that for every m, S_{M_T}(m)≤a(s(m)+S_T(m))^r and τ_{M_T}(m)≤b(s(m)+S_T(m)+τ_T(m))^r, with identical input lengths, exact output relation, and oracle convention. If T has S_T(m)≤s(m)^c and τ_T(m)≤s(m)^d for all m≥m₀, then M_T has S_{M_T}(m)≤s(m)^C₁ and τ_{M_T}(m)≤s(m)^C₂ for all sufficiently large m, for fixed exponents C₁,C₂. Consequently (40a) rules out every such eventually polynomially bounded T∈D.
derivation: Let k=max(c,d,1). For m≥max(m₀,2), s(m)≥m≥2, hence s(m)+S_T(m)≤2s(m)^k and s(m)+S_T(m)+τ_T(m)≤3s(m)^k. Thus S_{M_T}(m)≤a2^r s(m)^(kr) and τ_{M_T}(m)≤b3^r s(m)^(kr). Choose fixed integers C₁,C₂ large enough to absorb the constants into extra powers of s(m) for all sufficiently large m. Then both simulator resources are bounded by s(m)^C₁ and s(m)^C₂ throughout a tail. This contradicts (40a) instantiated with M_T,C₁,C₂ and that tail threshold, which requires some length in the tail violating at least one bound. Therefore no such T exists. This is conditional on the stated same-index exact simulation and matching oracle/resource hypotheses.

statement_start: Conditional index-transfer lemma: Let source lengths m range over the positive integers, let target lengths be f(m) with f(m) tending to infinity, and suppose a target streaming algorithm T has eventual polynomial resource bounds.
derivation: Let s(m) be the source parameter with s(m)>=m. Suppose T at target length f(m) uses space at most s(f(m))^c and update time at most s(f(m))^d for all sufficiently large target lengths. Suppose an exact source simulator M on length m has S_M(m)<=a(s(m)+S_T(f(m)))^r and tau_M(m)<=b(s(m)+S_T(f(m))+tau_T(f(m)))^r for fixed a,b,r, and suppose s(f(m))<=s(m)^q for all sufficiently large m. Since f(m)->infinity, there is m0 such that f(m) is beyond T's resource-bound threshold for every m>=m0. For such m, s(f(m))^c<=s(m)^(qc), and similarly for d. Set k=max(1,qc,qd). Then both simulator resource bounds are at most a(2s(m)^k)^r and b(3s(m)^k)^r. Since s(m)>=m tends to infinity, fixed multiplicative constants are absorbed by increasing the exponents, so S_M and tau_M are each bounded by a fixed power of s(m) for all sufficiently large m. Exact simulation preserves the problem's answer. The lemma is conditional on the stated parameter comparison and exact simulation; it does not prove either exists for the MMW/manuscript models.

proved_step: statement: Conditional oracle-elimination lemma. Fix A∈PH and suppose P=NP. Then the language Σ3SAT^A is in P. Consequently, any uniform streaming algorithm whose non-oracle transition work and oracle-query lengths are bounded by poly(s(m)) can replace each Σ3SAT^A query by a fixed uniform polynomial-time decider, yielding an oracle-free uniform algorithm with per-transition time poly(s(m)); its space is at most the original space plus the decider’s polynomial workspace in the query length. Proof: A∈PH implies Σ3SAT^A∈PH, since a fixed polynomial-hierarchy machine can make polynomially many queries to A∈PH and PH is closed under such oracle access. Under P=NP, PH=P, so the fixed language Σ3SAT^A has a uniform polynomial-time decider D. On each transition, simulate the original query construction and run D on the resulting query. If query length and transition construction time are poly(s(m)), D’s running time and workspace are also poly(s(m)); composing these procedures preserves uniformity and gives the stated bounds. This establishes oracle elimination only under the explicit query-size/resource premises; it does not yet verify those premises for MMW19 Thm 1.2 or close G0001.
